minutes.headline: Select Board leans toward passing over both TC Passios articles after cost estimates jumped; parcel sale fails 2-3
minutes.summary: The board heard a civics curriculum presentation, met the marijuana host community agreement applicant, and made routine appointments. The main item was the TC Passios renovation and new-build presentation after new cost estimates arrived that day; most members said they favored passing over both articles at the special town meeting, with no formal vote. The board declined to sell a town parcel, chose a landscape architect for 30 School Street, set a consent calendar, and a member announced his resignation.

votes.outcome: roll call taken; four ayes heard, final tally not stated

budget_items.what_was_said: Article for renovating the TC Passios into a town hall and community center was before the town at the earlier figure.
Alternative article would fund design development of a new building from free cash.
Estimates received that afternoon raised renovation about thirty percent and priced a new build far higher, citing material costs.
The town earlier allocated money to study a new build cost.
Design and engineering is billed as a percentage of project cost, with about forty percent spent before the decision point.
Delaying a decision adds cost each year, based on a construction cost index.
The finance committee chair estimated average household cost increases over 30 years and said the debt policy limit would be exceeded.
A member computed per-square-foot costs for the two options.
A bid below assessed value was discussed; the board declined to sell.
Fire chief received two grants for emergency planning and firefighter safety equipment.
Unitil winter rate increase was approved, and the aggregation rate was cited as an alternative.
Town manager noted there is no appropriation for the building, which runs on tenant rent, and added users risk a deficit to be addressed in the FY23 budget.
Price proposals from three firms were compared.

decisions.decision: Board will not vote on the TC Passios articles tonight; positions will be stated officially at town meeting, and the design committee will make its recommendation next Wednesday.
Board agreed to bring up a written nepotism policy for committee appointments and to consider reaching out to the affected person.
Board will not re-bid parcel 7 off Pratt Street again regardless of the vote outcome.
Host community agreement review deferred until after the November 16 special town meeting, aiming for execution before the holidays.

what_happened.line: Most Select Board members said they favored passing over both TC Passios articles at the special town meeting, but took no formal vote.
New cost estimates arrived the afternoon of the meeting, raising the renovation estimate and pricing a new build far higher, with material costs cited.
The board voted down the sale of parcel 7 off Pratt Street, with three members opposed, and said it will not re-bid the parcel.
The board awarded the 30 School Street landscape architecture proposal 4-1 and put six articles on the consent calendar unanimously.
The marijuana host community agreement review was deferred until after the November 16 special town meeting.

why_it_matters: The TC Passios articles decide whether the town hall and community center project goes forward, and the debt that follows would be paid mostly through property taxes.

Residents at the special town meeting will be asked to vote on these articles after the committees heard the new cost numbers only hours before, so the figures and the board's positions are worth reading first.
watch_next: The design committee's recommendation on the TC Passios articles, due the Wednesday after this meeting.
The November 16 special town meeting, where the board will state its positions and residents vote on the articles.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all five votes and their outcomes, and on most figures and the main decisions. Differences are mostly caption misrenderings of names and of the $39,000,637 estimate, plus items only one record has; the one to check is the nepotism-policy decision, which we describe more strongly than the official minutes do.
